content.title: Sports Illustrated
content.text: Michelle MarbryKentucky had control of the ball. He couldn’t call a timeout, plus the refs were moving down the floor with the play. They don’t have eyes in the back of their head. 15Vicki TravisCheck the rules he didn’t have a time out to call!4Chet WilliamsYes he is!! NCAA rules state, a coach cannot call a timeout if the ball is in the possession of the opponents hands, in which Aberdeen had possession!!9Kim Matthew BauerSendek was mad but it should have been at himself. He clearly hesitated too long. Plus his players had already started celebrating. If you look at the replay you'll see at least two of the defenders with their backs to the start of the last shot by Kentucky.5Tony BeamHe is dead wrong, when they hit the shot he should have been where the ball is getting put in bounds instead of celebrating and chasing a side judge down the court. You only have a couple seconds to call time out. Once the ball is inbounded you cant call a timeout without the ball, dead wrong, he knows the rules9LuAnn MooreThere are many videos out there that shows the tying basket was already made as the timeout was called Will CombsHe should have instructed his players to foul as soon as the ball was inbounded then the half court shot would have never happened.Instead all the players were running the court celebrating and the rest is history6Stephen HattonYou can’t call time out while the opponent has the ball. Owes had the ball in his hands dribbling before herb motioned for a timeout. Get over stop the narrative building.2Donald BrooksAll sports media is running this negative vibe. Wonder why? The ball was in UK player’s possession, the opposing team can not call for a timeout. The travel, arm chair refs have a luxury the refs don’t have.72
